# Research report

Claims: 8 verified, 0 partly supported, 13 total · Quotes: 13/15 matched · Sources: 2

## Conclusion

QPACK's static table has 99 entries indexed 0–98 (RFC 9204, Section 3.1 and Appendix A). Its encoder stream type is 0x02 and decoder stream type is 0x03 (RFC 9204, Section 4.2). RFC 9204 was published in June 2022 (RFC

9204 front matter). The largest QUIC variable-length integer is 2^62−1, or 4611686018427387903 (RFC 9000, Section 16). These authoritative figures correct conflicting values in notes.md.

## To do

1. **Proposal** Publish the short reference with the cited RFC sections and correct the four discrepant notes.md figures.
   <details>
   <summary>Related recommendations and sources</summary>

   Sources: [rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9204.html>), [rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9204/>), [rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9000.html>); rfc9204-001, rfc9204-002, source-rfc9204, source-001

   - **Proposal** Use the RFC-corrected figures above as the reference values and annotate the conflicting notes.md entries. (Sources: [rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9204.html>), [rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9204/>), [rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9000.html>); rfc9204-001, rfc9204-002, source-rfc9204, source-001)

   </details>

## Limits to keep in mind

- The supplied summary's table-size figure should not be used as the protocol value; the RFC identifies 99 entries.
- Using the notes' stream identifiers would swap the two protocol roles and produce an incorrect implementation reference.
- Use the official RFC publication month when dating or citing RFC 9204.
- The larger notes.md value is not encodable as a QUIC variable-length integer and must be replaced.

## Findings

### **Verified** RFC 9204's QPACK static table contains 99 entries indexed 0–98.

<details>
<summary>Evidence</summary>

- "Note that the QPACK static table is indexed from 0, whereas the HPACK static table is indexed from 1." — rfc9204-001 Section 3.1, lines 348–355
- "98  \| x-frame-options  \| sameorigin" — rfc9204-001 Appendix A, Table 4, lines 991–994

RFC 9204 Section 3.1 establishes zero-based indexing, and Appendix A lists index 98 as the final entry.

Confidence: High

Sources: [rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9204.html>); rfc9204-001, rfc9204-002, RFC 9204, Section 3.1, RFC 9204, Appendix A, Table 4

</details>

### **Verified** RFC 9204 Section 4.2 assigns unidirectional stream type 0x02 to the QPACK encoder stream.

<details>
<summary>Evidence</summary>

- "An encoder stream is a unidirectional stream of type 0x02." — source-rfc9204 lines 456-456

The RFC explicitly identifies the encoder stream type as 0x02.

Confidence: High

Sources: [rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9204.html>); source-rfc9204, RFC 9204, RFC Editor

</details>

### **Verified** RFC 9204 Section 4.2 assigns unidirectional stream type 0x03 to the QPACK decoder stream.

<details>
<summary>Evidence</summary>

- "A decoder stream is a unidirectional stream of type 0x03. It carries an unframed sequence of decoder instructions from decoder to encoder." — source-rfc9204

The RFC explicitly identifies the decoder stream type as 0x03.

Confidence: High

Sources: [rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9204.html>); source-rfc9204, RFC 9204, RFC Editor

</details>

### **Verified** RFC 9204 was published in June 2022.

<details>
<summary>Evidence</summary>

- "Published:\\n    June 2022" — RFC Editor

The RFC front matter and official RFC metadata provide the June 2022 publication month.

Confidence: High

Sources: [rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9204.html>), [rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9204/>); source-001, RFC Editor

</details>

### **Verified** The largest encodable QUIC variable-length integer is 4611686018427387903, equal to 2^62−1.

<details>
<summary>Evidence</summary>

- "11  \| 8  \| 62 \| 0-4611686018427387903" — RFC 9000, Section 16, Table 4 lines 1915-1915

RFC 9000 Section 16 gives the 62-bit maximum value.

Confidence: High

Sources: [rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9000.html>); source-001, RFC 9000, Section 16, Table 4

</details>

- notes.md states that RFC 9204 was published in June 2021. Correction: RFC 9204 was published in June 2022. ([rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9204.html>); notes.md, source-notes, local repository, `notes.md`, RFC Editor)

</details>

([rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9204.txt>), [rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9204.html>); notes.md, local-notes-001, rfc9204-001, rfc9204-002)
- notes.md reverses the encoder and decoder stream-type assignments; RFC 9204 assigns 0x02 to the encoder and 0x03 to the decoder. ([rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9204.html>); <cwd>/notes.md, source-local-notes, source-rfc9204)
- notes.md gives June 2021, while official RFC metadata and front matter identify June 2022. ([rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9204.html>), [rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9204/>); notes.md, source-notes, source-001)
- notes.md gives 2^64−1, but RFC 9000 defines the maximum QUIC variable-length integer as 2^62−1. ([rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9000.html>); notes.md, source-002, source-001)

</details>

<details>
<summary>Unverified lead (11)</summary>

- RFC 9204 Sections 4.2 and 8.2 provide the stream-type citation anchor. ([rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9204.html>); source-rfc9204)

- The supplied notes.md figures require correction against RFC 9204 and RFC 9000. ([rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9204.html>), [rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9000.html>); source-notes, source-rfc9204, source-rfc9000)
- RFC 9204 defines two QPACK unidirectional stream types. ([rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9204.html>); source-rfc9204)
- notes.md lines 3–6 contain the four supplied figures used for cross-checking. (source-notes)
- RFC 9204 states that the QPACK static table is indexed from 0. ([rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9204.html>); rfc9204-001)
- RFC 9204 Appendix A lists the final QPACK static-table entry at index 98. ([rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9204.html>); rfc9204-002)
- RFC 9204's QPACK static table has 99 entries indexed from 0 through 98. ([rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9204.html>); rfc9204-001, rfc9204-002)
- The largest encodable QUIC variable-length integer is 4611686018427387903, equal to 2^62−1. ([rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9000.html>); source-001)
- RFC 9000 defines QUIC variable-length integers with 6-, 14-, 30-, or 62-bit values. ([rfc-editor.org](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9000.html>); source-001)

</details>
